story:
Before the war every body the colleges sent across to Caldey came wrapped, and somebody had to sew the wrapping. For most of forty years that was Rose. She sewed in the long room behind her cottage in Little Haven with three needles going, a coarse one for the hem and a fine one for the seam and a third, a bone needle her mother left her, for a single stitch she put into every shroud she made, at the left shoulder, which she said was so that the dead would know whose work they were wearing and lie still out of courtesy.

They did not lie still. When the witch called and the isle stood up, half the dead who stood up were wearing Rose's shrouds, and the ghostly ones still are: pale, soft, drifting things that walk the isle in the linen she hemmed. Little Haven says she took it harder than anyone. She did not weep. She sat down in the long room and worked out, from her own book, how many she had sewn, and then she went to Mordwywr and asked him to enter in his ledger that she would pay for every one brought back to her.

She pays still. The realm's young bring her the ghostly shrouds off the walking dead, and she turns each one over and finds her stitch at the left shoulder, and puts it in the chest in the long room, and pays. She has never once found a shroud without her stitch. Mordwywr has written in the ledger that he believes she would pay for one of someone else's, if it came, out of respect for the other seamstress; it has not come.

Rose has never raised a hand to anyone in Little Haven or out of it, and the young who bring her shrouds are as safe in her long room as in a chapel. The clan's defenders on the wall above the village count her among their own, and the fishermen say nobody on Caldey would be fool enough to find out what happens to someone who harms the shroud-woman.
legend: Rose is a level 54 villager of Little Haven on Caldey who buys Ghostly Soul Shrouds (her turn-in, levels 46 to 48). She is not hostile: her faction, the Caldey Outpost, starts neutral, and she leaves players of her quest's level band alone in any case. There is nothing to gain by killing her and a lot to lose: the clan's barbarian defenders share her faction and come in, and it sours your standing with the clan and the outpost's merchants. No spells or styles in the data. She is a named 54, so the realm counts her; bring her shrouds instead.

loremasterTopic.text: The shroud-woman of [little haven], who sewed the wrapping of most of the college dead sent to [caldey] for forty years, with one stitch of her own at every left shoulder so that the dead would lie still out of courtesy. When the isle stood up they walked in her linen. She pays for every ghostly shroud brought back, and has never found one without her stitch.

bookPage: From the Ledger of Little Haven, kept by Mordwywr, enchanter. Paid by Rose, to a young friar of the realm, for one ghostly shroud: the usual. Rose turned it over, found her stitch, and sat a while. She said this one was a master of the college of stars, a tall man, she remembered the length of linen. She said he had asked her once, when he came to see the isle, whether a shroud could be sewn so that the dead would stay down for certain. She had told him no. She said she had been right, and that she had never wanted so much to be wrong. I have entered the payment and not the rest.
